data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Popper's preference for the better-corroborated theory is defensible on his own terms as a methodological rule of 'critical preference' rather than an inductive inference; it survives by redefining rational action as the selection of the hypothesis with the highest informational content and severest test history, accepting the cost that this preference offers no guarantee of future success or increased probability of truth, only the status of being the most rationally criticizable option currently available.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the preference for the better-corroborated theory implicitly assumes that the future will resemble the past (uniformity of nature), then it smuggles in induction.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If Popper's concept of 'verisimilitude' (truth-likeness) cannot be formally defined without logical contradiction (as shown by Tich\u00fd and Miller), then the justification for preferring one theory over another collapses.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If acting on a theory inherently requires assigning it a higher subjective probability of success than its rivals, then the distinction between corroboration and probability is merely semantic.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The argument distinguishes between 'justification' (seeking probability/induction) and 'criticism' (seeking error elimination). It posits that preferring Theory A over B is not a claim that A is more likely true, but a procedural decision that A has withstood tests that would have falsified B, making A the better target for future criticism and the only non-arbitrary choice for action in the absence of certainty. This relies on the asymmetry of falsification: while corroboration doesn't prove truth, failed falsification attempts eliminate competitors, leaving the survivor as the pragmatic choice without invoking the uniformity of nature.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
